title: 264 - River City Ransom
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: River City Ransom
items.description: The episode's game: an open-world beat-'em-up with RPG-style shopping, set in River City, released by Technos.

items.name: Kunio-kun
items.description: The Japanese Technos series the hosts say River City Ransom, Renegade and Super Dodge Ball all come from.

items.name: Renegade
items.description: Earlier Technos NES beat-'em-up from the Kunio-kun series, covered previously on the show.

items.name: Super Dodge Ball
items.description: Earlier Technos NES sports game from the Kunio-kun series, also set in River City.

items.name: Technos Japan
items.description: Developer of River City Ransom, Double Dragon, Renegade and Super Dodge Ball.

links.label: Wikipedia: Technōs Japan
links.note: Japanese video game developer and publisher

items.name: Riverdale
items.description: The CW teen drama based on Archie Comics, joked about because of the River City name.

items.name: Archie Comics
items.description: Publisher of the comics that Riverdale is based on.

items.name: Arrested Development
items.description: TV comedy mentioned in a joke about characters checking themselves into jail.

items.name: Persona
items.description: The Atlus series known for high-school life simulation, referenced as a different kind of high school game.

items.name: Retro City Rampage
items.description: A 2012 parody game of 80s pop culture, the only other similarly named game one host recalled.

items.name: Super Mario Bros.
items.description: Used as a comparison for how early games were linked into a shared universe.

items.name: Double Dragon
items.description: Technos's other beat-'em-up, compared for enemy design and its two-enemy-at-a-time limit.

items.name: Double Dragon II: The Revenge
items.description: Previous Double Dragon episode game, and one of the games in the PC Engine collection.

links.label: Wikipedia: Double Dragon II: The Revenge (NES video game)

items.name: Yakuza
items.description: Sega action-adventure series compared for buying food and items to boost stats.

items.name: The Warriors
items.description: 1979 film about rival street gangs, compared to River City Ransom's themed gangs.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Warriors (film)
links.note: 1979 American action thriller film by Walter Hill

items.name: EarthBound
items.description: RPG cited for its everyday, normal-world setting with game mechanics layered on top.

items.name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
items.description: Used as a joke about role-playing strictly, like waiting to be bitten by a vampire.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim

items.name: Simon Belmont
items.description: The whip-wielding Castlevania hero, referenced when talking about the long chain weapon.

items.name: GameFAQs
items.description: Game guide site that lists River City Ransom's item stats.

items.name: Sharp X68000
items.description: Japanese home computer that received an enhanced port with three enemies on screen.

items.name: Nintendo 64DD
items.description: Japan-only disk drive add-on for the N64, brought up as a comparison.

items.name: Super NES CD-ROM
items.description: The canceled Nintendo and Sony CD add-on, the so-called Nintendo PlayStation.

items.name: TurboGrafx-16
items.description: The North American name of the PC Engine.

items.name: Sega CD
items.description: CD add-on for the Genesis, compared to the PC Engine Super CD-ROM.

items.name: Game Boy Advance
items.description: Nintendo handheld that got River City Ransom EX and sparked a closing debate.

items.name: Ben 10
items.description: Cartoon the hosts compare the EX box art style to.

items.name: Samurai Jack
items.description: Cartoon the hosts compare the EX box art style to.

items.name: ChatGPT
items.description: AI chatbot joked about as a computer-controlled co-op partner.

items.name: Game Boy
items.description: Nintendo's original handheld, compared with the Game Boy Advance in the closing debate.

items.name: Nintendo DS
items.description: Handheld one host looks at more fondly than the Game Boy Advance.
